title: Finite endpoint cone comparison
statement: Finite endpoint cone comparison for the vertical tower equals the totalized vertical window homology.

source.place: Proof steps 1 and 2, first sequence: Homology of a totalized cutoff cone equals smart vertical interval homology

proof.text: Construct the natural map between finite smart cutoff functors using the inverse truncation inclusion on the smaller cutoff. Whisker with extension and restriction, and apply it columnwise to K. Its composite with the b-cutoff inclusion is the a-cutoff inclusion. Degreewise monicity gives Mono f. Form the canonical cokernel short exact sequence.

Apply exactness of extended first-quadrant totalization. The totalized first map equals the chosen tower map: both factor the a-tower inclusion through the monomorphic b-tower inclusion. Mathlib CochainComplex.mappingCone.quasiIso_descShortComplex now identifies cone homology with the homology of the extended total cokernel.

Use the columnwise cutoff quotient comparison to obtain q from the bicomplex cokernel to the smart window, with every q.f p a quasi-isomorphism. Apply the generic vertical cone filtration to the extended total map of q. Negative graded pieces are zero; nonnegative graded pieces have the homology of the extended column-map cones. Mathlib extension preserves quasi-isomorphisms, and its cone criterion makes each such cone acyclic.

Degreewise finite filtered acyclicity makes the total-map cone acyclic. The cone criterion gives a quasi-isomorphism from the extended total cokernel to the extended total window. Compose its homology isomorphism with the short-exact cone comparison, in the order cone -> total cokernel -> total window.

proof_origin.place: Finite endpoint case: canonical cutoff lift, totalized cokernel sequence, column quotient comparison, and finite cone filtration; Lean reduction by B2

Short exact truncation and cone homology APIs found; the finite-diagonal totalization comparison remains to formalize.
